summary: Temporary cross-cloud IAM chaining and service-account impersonation for finance/analytics billing reconciliation
description:
Issue summary:
Request from Finance/Analytics to run a one-off billing reconciliation job that requires access to production cloud billing exports and node-level metrics across both AWS and GCP accounts. The analytics team needs temporary ability to assume an AWS cross-account role and impersonate a GCP service account from our platform account so they can pull aggregated billing CSVs and validate cost allocation logic.

Impact:
- Blocking: Finance cannot complete month-end reconciliation until dataset pull is validated.
- Risk: Granting overly-broad privileges could expose billing data or allow lateral movement. Security needs least-privilege, timebound access.

Background / Justification:
- Job: analytics/billing-recon/2026-03-month-end (ad-hoc Spark job run from analytics internal tooling).
- Justification: Audit request and discrepancy flagged by finance (see Slack thread #finance-billing, message ts: 2026-03-09).
- Requested duration: 48 hours with automatic revocation.

Requested scope (least-privilege):
- AWS: Allow sts:AssumeRole into role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-billing-readonly-crossaccount with policy limited to s3:GetObject on buckets: prod-billing-exports-us-west and prod-cluster-metrics-us-west. No EC2 or secrets access.
- GCP: Allow impersonation of service account redwood-billing-reader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com with roles/storage.objectViewer and roles/bigquery.dataViewer only for the billing project.
- Access method: Requestor will run a signed short-lived session via internal CLI which must authenticate with SSO; RBAC gating enforced.

Approval path and auditors:
- Approvers: Security (Jenna Li), Cloud Infra (Marco Ruiz), Finance (Daniel Romero).
- Audit requirements: Record assume-role events and service-account tokens in Cloud Audit Logs and CloudTrail.

Next steps requested from Infra/Security team:
1) Create the cross-account AWS role with constrained trust policy (only allow assume from analytics-internal SAML principal).
2) Patch IAM bindings on GCP to add iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to the analytics-runner group for the specific service account, scoped to billing project.
3) Attach a timebound condition or schedule cleanup job to remove bindings after 48 hours.
4) Provide documented CLI commands and monitoring dashboards for the requestor.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Login to internal analytics bastion with SSO (okta).
2. Run internal CLI: redwood auth assume-aws --role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-billing-readonly-crossaccount
4. Run gcloud auth application-default impersonate-service-account redwood-billing-reader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com -- gcloud storage objects list --bucket prod-billing-exports-us-west
logs:
Example denied event (CloudTrail): 2026-03-09T14:22:10Z AccessDenied sts:AssumeRole Caller=arn:aws:iam::444455556666:user/analytics-runner Resource=arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-billing-readonly-crossaccount
GCP denied: 2026-03-09T14:25:03Z serviceAccountTokenCreator denied for principal analytics-runner@redwood.internal
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Filing request on behalf of Finance. Attached Slack thread and initial CSV showing discrepancy. Requesting 48-hour window.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Jenna Li (Security): Can you confirm exact principals that need the role and whether the job will run from CI or interactive terminal? We require SSO-based principal mapping and MFA.
2026-03-10 10:42 - Aisha Patel: Job will be kicked off interactively by two analysts (dan.romero, liam.kim) from analytics bastion. They will use internal CLI which enforces MFA.

2026-03-10 13:30 - Marco Ruiz (Infra): I will prepare a scoped role and post a Terraform change. Planning to allow s3:GetObject only on the two buckets and to add condition aws:RequestTag/RequestOrigin=finance-recon. Need security to sign off on tag-based condition.
2026-03-11 08:20 - Jenna Li (Security): Approved with condition. Security requests CloudTrail + Logging retention set to 90 days for these events and notification to #sec-audit on first use.
2026-03-11 12:05 - Marco Ruiz (Infra): Terraform PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2782. Created AWS role in staging for smoke tests; GCP binding requires org-policy check.

2026-03-12 07:10 - Marco Ruiz: Confirmed staged smoke test succeeded. Created TimeBound access via IAM Conditions; scheduled cleanup job in infra-scheduler. Marking as In Progress while we await production deploy (PR linked).
investigation_notes: Initial reproduction showed two distinct failures: AWS returned AccessDenied on sts:AssumeRole due to trust policy that referenced the wrong SAML provider ARN; GCP blocked iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator due to a restrictive organization policy that only allows impersonation from members of a specific group (analytics-runner-prod) which the analysts were not in. Verified CloudTrail and Cloud Audit Logs for 2026-03-09 events. Hypothesis: misconfiguration during previous org-wide tightening of impersonation rules. Temporary solution: add analysts to analytics-runner-prod group OR create a narrowly-scoped proxy role with explicit principal identity and very limited permissions. Long-term: add runbook for cross-cloud temporary access pattern and automation to request timebound access with audit hooks.
resolution_notes: Provisioned role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-billing-readonly-crossaccount with limited s3:GetObject and explicit trust for Okta SAML principal 'analytics-sso'. Applied condition aws:RequestTag/RequestOrigin=finance-recon and created an IAM role session policy limiting access to the two billing buckets. On GCP, granted iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to group analytics-runner-prod for redwood-billing-reader@redwood-prod and added the two analysts as members. Terraform PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/8f3b2c1. Cleanup automation scheduled: infra-scheduler job 'revoke-temp-billing-access-12890' will run 48 hours after the production deploy. Audit hooks: CloudTrail and Cloud Audit Logs forwarded to splunk index 'access-audit' and a first-use alert posted to #sec-audit. Ticket to remain open until revocation job completes and audit confirms no anomalous activity.
